Title: Four detained in suspected illegal gold mining operation
Article:
news@nst.com.my
Pix courtesy of GOF
GUA MUSANG: Three Malaysians and a Chinese citizen were detained during a raid on a suspected illegal gold mining operation in Jalan Masjid RPK, Kuala Betis, here yesterday.
General Operations Force Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the four men, aged between 19 and 64, were detained during the operation at 4pm.
He said the operation was carried out by the brigade's intelligence team following information on suspected illegal gold mining activities, with assistance from the Bukit Aman Air Operations Team and Kelantan Land and Mines Office enforcement officers.
"Upon arrival, the team found the entrance gate to the premises locked from inside. The team then entered the area to conduct an inspection.
"Four men were found in front of a shed in suspicious circumstances," he said in a statement.
Ahmad Radzi said checks found that three of the men were Malaysians while the fourth was a Chinese citizen who was in possession of a valid passport.
He said no contraband was found during body searches on the four suspects.
However, he added that further checks of the premises uncovered equipment believed to have been used for gold mining, including two excavators, two sluice boxes, two suction machines and two generator sets.
"The team also found a locked yellow container containing 51 pieces of grass carpet of various sizes and three rolls of grass carpet, which were believed to be related to the illegal operation.
"Based on preliminary investigations, the activities at the location are suspected to involve the misuse of an application or permit related to sand extraction for the purpose of carrying out gold mining activities.
"The seized equipment and materials were estimated to be worth RM1.135 million," he said.
They comprised two excavators worth about RM1 million, two sluice boxes (RM60,000), two suction machines (RM25,000), two generator sets (RM25,000), 51 pieces of grass carpet (RM10,200) and three rolls of grass carpet (RM15,000).
"No minerals or gold were seized during the operation," he said.
He added that all four suspects were detained to assist in investigations, while the equipment was handed over to the Kelantan PTG for further action.
Ahmad Radzi said the case was being investigated under Section 158 of the Kelantan Mineral Enactment 2001 for suspected mining without a valid licence or lease, as well as the alleged misuse of documents or applications related to sand extraction.

Title: Ten undocumented migrants escape from Tanah Merah detention depot
Article:
KOTA BARU: Ten undocumented migrants escaped from the Immigration detention depot in Tanah Merah early today, prompting police to launch an operation to track them down.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the escapees comprised seven Thai citizens, an Indonesian, a Bangladeshi and a Rohingya.
"Police launched Ops Tutup this morning to locate and recapture all 10 escapees," he said.
Yusoff urged members of the public who spot anyone matching their description not to approach them but to immediately contact the police.
The escapees are believed to be wearing bright green shirts issued by the detention depot and are reportedly bald.
Those with information can contact the Tanah Merah district police headquarters at 09-9556222, Tanah Merah police station at 09-9556223 or the District Control Centre via WhatsApp at 011-29555518.

Title: Orang Asli youth killed after motorcycle hits civet, crashes into SUV
Article:
ROMPIN: An Orang Asli youth was killed after his motorcycle hit a civet before crashing into an SUV at Km23 of Jalan Ibam-Rompin here yesterday.
Zaki Abu, 19, a plantation worker from Kampung Gadak, Muadzam Shah, died at the scene in the 8.40pm accident.
District police chief Superintendent Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said the accident involved Zaki's Honda motorcycle and an SUV driven by a 40-year-old plantation assistant manager.
"The SUV was travelling from Rompin towards Ibam, while Zaki was riding in the opposite direction.
"Zaki is believed to have hit a civet, causing his motorcycle to veer into the opposite lane and collide with the oncoming SUV," he said in a statement today.
He said Zaki died at the scene, while the SUV driver was unhurt.
The carcass of the civet was found on the road.
He said the case was being investigated for death by reckless or dangerous driving.

Title: Umno to send representative to Pas Muktamar, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno has confirmed it will send a representative to the 72nd Pas Muktamar in Kelantan next month.
Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, however, did not name the representative, saying the party would decide on the matter later.
"We will definitely send a representative to the muktamar," he said briefly when asked about Pas' invitation.
Yesterday, Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan confirmed that invitations had been extended to Zahid and three other Umno leaders to attend the annual gathering.
Takiyuddin, who is also Kota Baru member of parliament, said Pas had yet to receive a response from Umno over the invitations.
The 72nd Pas Muktamar is scheduled to be held in Kelantan on Sept 4, with its party president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang expected to deliver the opening address.

Title: MEF: Digital foreign worker system must deliver results, not just go paperless
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The digitalisation of foreign worker recruitment must deliver real improvements, not merely replace paper forms with online ones, the Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) said.
President Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman said digitalising applications through the Foreign Workers Centralised Management System (FWCMS) was a step in the right direction, but its success would depend on execution.
"It should fundamentally improve the efficiency, transparency and predictability of the entire process," he said in a statement.
Syed Hussain said the goal should be a "one application, one system, one status" approach, where employers need not repeatedly submit the same information to different agencies or make physical visits just to check an application's status.
MEF proposed six measures to ensure the system delivers its intended improvements.
These include end-to-end application tracking, clear service-level timelines with a 14-day approval window for complete applications, single document submission across agencies, strong technical capacity and cybersecurity safeguards, a responsive helpdesk for escalations, and continuous engagement between government and industry associations to identify bottlenecks and improve user experience.
Syed Hussain said predictability was especially important for micro, small and medium enterprises, which needed to know how long the process would take, what requirements they had to meet, and what to do when an application encountered a problem.
Meanwhile, MEF also backed the government's phased approach to foreign worker quota allocation, including for the restaurant sector.
Syed Hussain said a monitored rollout would help align recruitment with actual labour market needs while allowing the government to track compliance and quota utilisation.
Employers seeking to recruit foreign workers no longer need to submit applications manually or make walk-in visits to government offices, with the
entire process conducted online
through FWCMS beginning yesterday.
The ministry said the process begins with employers obtaining prior approval to hire foreign workers under Section 60K of the Employment Act 1955 and ends with the issuance of a Conditional Approval Letter (SKB).
The SKB can be obtained within 14 days, subject to complete applications and compliance with stipulated requirements and criteria.
Employers can access FWCMS through [www.fwcms.com.my] (http://www.fwcms.com.my).
The ministry also said a phased quota allocation approach was being implemented to facilitate employers' applications following the opening of a quota for 15,000 foreign workers in the restaurant industry, as announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on July 24.

Title: Malaysia Smelting mine suspension seen temporary, no outlook hit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Smelting Corp Bhd's (MSC) temporary suspension of mining operations is unlikely to derail its overall outlook, according to Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest).
Analyst Denny Oh said the suspension at MSC's 80 per cent-owned Rahman Hydraulic Tin Sdn Bhd in Perak was a temporary operational setback.
He said the earnings impact would depend largely on how long the suspension lasts.
"Based on a preliminary estimates, assuming a three-week stoppage and a 25 per cent drop in Rahman Hydraulic Tin's quarterly output, the mining segment could see a pre-tax profit loss of roughly RM15 million to RM20 million," he said in a note.
He added that this could reduce PublicInvest's earnings forecast for the financial year 2026 by 11 per cent to 15 per cent.
However, Oh said the impact would be partly cushioned by MSC's tin smelting operations, which remain unaffected as the company can source ore from other mines.
"The tin smelting operations are not affected, as they can source ore from other mines, which would partially compensate for the lost volume from Rahman Hydraulic Tin," he said.
Rahman Hydraulic Tin's mining operations were suspended on August12 following a directive from the Perak Department of Minerals and Geosciences after about 60mm of rain fell within an hour on August 3.
The rainfall exceeded the mine's drainage and retention pond infrastructure design intensity of 50 mm, resulting in damage and overwhelmed ponds.
Rahman Hydraulic Tin has started repair and upgrading works and is working with Perak Minerals and the Geoscience Department on a remedial action plan.
The suspension will remain until further notice from the authorities.
Despite the disruption, Oh maintained a positive view on MSC, citing his continued optimism over the tin market and the company's prospects.
PublicInvest kept its earnings forecasts unchanged for now, pending further discussions with management.
The firm maintained its "Outperform" call and RM3.10 target price for MSC, based on 18 times FY27 forecast earnings per share.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malakoff recovery clouded by tax hit; analysts split on outlook
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malakoff Corp Bhd's earnings recovery is gaining traction following improved plant operations, but analysts remain divided on the outlook as higher taxes and non-recurring gains cloud its underlying performance.
RHB Research analyst Max Koh said Malakoff's financial year 2026 earnings estimates had been cut by 45 per cent to account for a higher effective tax rate (ETR) of 40 per cent, compared with 19 per cent previously.
He said management had attributed the 51 per cent ETR in the second quarter of financial year 2026 (Q2 FY26) mainly to non-tax-deductible expenses related to its sukuk.
"We have adopted a prudent approach by applying a 40 per cent ETR for FY26F," Koh said, adding that the ETR assumptions for FY27 and FY28 had also been raised to 28 per cent from 21 per cent.
Koh said the Malakoff's operational recovery remained on track, particularly with the 350 megawatt (MW) Prai power plant performing above expectations following the extension of its power purchase agreement (PPA) in April.
Prai achieved an energy availability factor of 91 per cent and a capacity factor of 30 per cent in Q2 FY26, contributing RM90 million to group revenue during the quarter.
RHB Research has consequently raised its FY26 capacity factor assumption for Prai to 20 per cent from nine per cent and expects it to rise to 30 per cent in FY27 and FY28.
Koh said earnings from Malakoff's Tanjung Bin Power Plant (TBP) are expected to improve in the second half of FY26 following the resumption of rotor operations this month.
"We also expect the reset of TBP's unscheduled outage rate in 2027 to result in full capacity payments," he said.
RHB Research maintained its "Buy" call on the power producer while lowering its target price to RM1 from RM1.06, citing improving contributions from the Prai power plant and expectations of a stronger performance in FY27.
Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest), however, retained its "Underperform" call with a target price of 74 sen, saying it remained cautious until Malakoff demonstrates stable plant availability and recurring earnings.
Its analyst Khairul Fahmi said Malakoff's operational recovery had become more encouraging, with the entire Tanjung Bin Complex returning to full baseload on Aug 9.
However, he noted that Q2 FY26 headline profit after tax and minority interest (Patami) of RM31.7 million was supported by RM48 million in insurance claims and a RM20 million arbitration gain from its Shuaibah associates.
Excluding these items, core loss after tax and minority interest (Latami) narrowed to RM36.3 million from RM77.7 million in the first quarter, bringing the first-half (1H) FY26 core Latami to RM114 million.
"This implies that Malakoff would need to deliver core Patami of RM173.5 million in 2H FY26 to meet our FY26F estimate of RM59.5 million," Khairul said.
He said further insurance proceeds were expected from the third quarter of FY26 onwards, but PublicInvest would continue to exclude the recoveries from core earnings as they were non-recurring.
Malakoff received about RM130 million in insurance proceeds during 1H FY26, comprising around RM80 million related to TBP and RM50 million linked to the Tanjung Bin Energy fire incident.
Khairul also highlighted stronger contributions from Malakoff's gas assets, with Segari Energy Ventures recording a 31 per cent capacity factor against management's 5.0 per cent target, while Prai achieved 30 per cent against a 20 per cent target.
"The management guided that the absence of an interim dividend was due to cash preservation for the upcoming projects in the pipeline while maintaining its full-year payout guidance of 70 per cent of consolidated Patami," he said.
Looking ahead, both analysts pointed to Malakoff's project pipeline as an important longer-term catalyst.
RHB Research said Malakoff's plan to develop two new 1.4 gigawatt (GW) gas-fired plants in Port Dickson, Negri Sembilan, and Segari, Perak, could support earnings growth as TBP's PPA is due to expire in September 2031.
Koh estimated that winning a bid for a new 1.4GW plant could result in a 42 per cent accretion to RHB Research's target price.
PublicInvest said Malakoff's renewable projects, including the 84MW Sungai Galas small-hydro portfolio, the 470MW LSS5+ project and the 100MW Bintulu solar project, remained on track.
However, it said the near-term earnings contribution from these projects remained limited, leaving the recovery of existing thermal assets as the key earnings driver for 2H FY26.

Title: Johor Plantations earnings tied to 2H output recovery, CPO prices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Plantations Group Bhd's (JPG) earnings outlook is expected to hinge on a recovery in fresh fruit bunches (FFB) production in the second half (2H) of 2026 and sustained crude palm oil (CPO) prices, following a weaker-than-expected first-half performance.
RHB Research analyst Hoe Lee Leng said JPG's FFB production was expected to recover in 2H in line with the seasonal production peak, while higher CPO prices would be positive for the group given its high sensitivity to movements in CPO prices.
JPG has revised its FFB production target to about one million tonnes for financial years 2026 and 2027 (FY26-27), with a 40:60 production split between the first and second halves.
RHB Research adjusted its FY26-28 earnings forecasts down by 14.5 per cent for FY26, while raising them by five per cent for FY27 and 2.8 per cent for FY28, reflecting lower FFB growth, a reduced ASP premium over MPOB's reference price, downstream losses, higher interest income and costs, and lower administrative costs.
"We also impute updated FY27-28 CPO price assumptions of RM4,500-4,400 a tonne from RM4,300 previously and our latest in-house foreign exchange assumptions," Hoe said in a note.
She maintained a "Buy" call on JPG and raised its target price to RM2.20 from RM1.90, citing expectations of a seasonal recovery in FFB output and stronger CPO prices.
However, Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) analyst Chye Wen Fei downgraded the stock to "Hold" from "Buy", while maintaining its target price at RM1.78, saying the recent share price outperformance had run ahead of fundamentals.
Chye said JPG's weaker-than-expected earnings had prompted it to lower its FY26 and FY27 core earnings forecasts by 15 per cent and 7.7 per cent, respectively.
The cuts mainly reflected lower FFB yield assumptions, partly offset by higher average CPO price assumptions following earlier sector-wide upward revisions.
She said 1H FY26 core earnings of RM91.4 million, down 36.1 per cent year-on-year, accounted for only 27.2 per cent to 30.8 per cent of consensus and HLIB Research's full-year estimates.
The shortfall was mainly due to lower-than-expected FFB production.
JPG's 1H FFB output fell 11.3 per cent to 420,478 tonnes, mainly due to reduced harvesting areas following its accelerated replanting programme and weaker yields caused by prolonged moisture stress.
Management expects FFB production to recover in 2H, although Chye estimates FY26 output could still decline about 9.0 per cent from FY25 due to reduced mature areas and weaker yields.
On its downstream expansion, HLIB said construction of JPG's Ispoc complex was 84 per cent complete as of June 2026.
The renewable energy plant is expected to be commissioned in Q3 2026, followed by the refinery and palm oil mill in Q4 2026, while the kernel crushing plant and animal feed mill are targeted for commissioning in FY27.
"Management expects Ispoc to register a small loss in FY26 and only start contributing positively to JPG from FY27, with a targeted profit after tax margin of eight per cent to 10 per cent on estimated annual revenue of about RM750 million upon full ramp-up," she added.

Title: Shifting from 'Made in Malaysia' to 'Made by Malaysians'
Article:
KUCHING: Malaysia needs to shift from being merely a production base to becoming a country that creates and owns content and intellectual property (IP) to ensure its digital creative industry remains competitive regionally and globally.
Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) chief executive officer Anuar Fariz Fadzil said Malaysia could no longer rely on competitive costs as its main strategy to attract and retain the digital content industry. Instead, the country must focus on excellence, quality, innovation, talent and developing local IP with commercial value in international markets.
"Our future lies in driving excellence, producing high-quality works and building value from the talent and creativity of Malaysians," he said at the "Building a Sustainable Ecosystem for the Digital Content Revolution" session on the third day of the Borneo Animation & Games Festival (BAGFest) 2026 at the Pullman Hotel Kuching.
The session also featured Sarawak Digital Economy Corporation (SDEC) chief executive officer Datuk Sudarnoto Osman and Enfiniti Group president and chief dream maker Puan Sri Tiara Jacquelina Eu Effendi, with discussions covering talent development, funding opportunities, technological innovation and regional collaboration.
Anuar said Malaysia's strengths included competitive operating costs, English proficiency, local talent and infrastructure capable of supporting international companies.
However, he said being a low-cost production base would not be sufficient in the long term, particularly as regional countries developed their own capabilities.
As such, he stressed the need for Malaysia to move up the value chain of the digital creative industry.
"We need to shift from 'Made in Malaysia' to 'Made by Malaysians'. The question is no longer simply where the content is produced, but who creates it, who owns the IP and who benefits from its economic value."
Anuar said Malaysia's experience as an outsourcing base over several decades should not be viewed as a disadvantage. Instead, the period had given the local workforce opportunities to develop skills, gain experience and be exposed to international production standards.
"Now, we need to translate that experience into the creation of our own IP," he said, adding that the process had helped produce a more mature workforce capable of creating its own animation, games and creative content.
Anuar also stressed that the digital content industry should not be viewed solely through its end products. Instead, each production forms part of a wider economic chain involving producers, scriptwriters, designers, production crews, prop makers, costume providers, financiers and various support services.
"When a production grows, it does not just create a film or a game. It creates jobs, builds skills and drives the entire creative economy," he said.
BAGFest 2026, which runs from Aug 19 to today at the Pullman Hotel Kuching and The Hills Kuching, is among the platforms bringing together studios, producers, investors, talent, students and industry players from Malaysia and abroad.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police probe viral video of motorcyclists allegedly racing on Linkedua Highway
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are investigating a viral video showing two motorcyclists allegedly racing each other along the Linkedua Highway yesterday.
Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) said a report was received regarding the incident, which is believed to have occurred from the Senai Utara Toll Interchange towards the JPO Interchange.
"A person believed to have been at the scene has been identified.
"The Kulai TEID is conducting investigations to identify the motorcyclists and other individuals who were at the scene.
"Police have also contacted PLUS Malaysia Bhd to obtain closed-circuit television camera recordings from the location," it said in a statement.
Previously, a
30-second video

Title: The man who built tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Long before Malaysia–China trade emerged as a cornerstone of regional commerce, a self-made entrepreneur from Muar was already paving the way.
Tan Sri Lim Kim Hong inspired some of Malaysia's most iconic names, from Tan Sri Robert Kuok's sprawling empire to household pillars including Malayan Banking Bhd, Permodalan Nasional Bhd and Tan Chong Motors, as they expanded into the world's most dynamic market.
A visionary, founder of i-City and one of Malaysia's most accomplished business leaders, Lim was building economic bridges between the two nations at a time when few Malaysian entrepreneurs dared venture into China.
His life mirrors Malaysia's own journey: from a carpenter's workbench in Johor to building cities of the future; from opening new frontiers abroad to leading the nation into an AI-powered era.
His trajectory, from humble beginnings to building cross-border ties, embodies the Merdeka spirit: that resilience, boldness and devotion to one's nation can shape a country's destiny, whatever one's origins.
From Muar's Carpentry Shops to a Millionaire at 18
Born into a large, struggling family in Muar, Johor, Lim learned hardship early. His father died when he was young; his mother supported the household, earning just RM2 a day at a rubber processing factory. He attended Chung Hwa Primary School but completed only six years of formal education. At 12, unable to continue his studies, he left school to apprentice at a furniture factory.
By 16 he was a master carpenter, yet his vision stretched far beyond timber and joinery. By 18, his furniture business had earned him his first million ringgit.
At 21, he turned a distribution deal for Dunlop mattresses into Malaysia's largest network, then launched the Dreamland spring mattress brand, revolutionising how Malaysians slept and earning him the enduring title of the "Mattress King".
Opening China's Doors for Malaysian Enterprise
In 1984, Tan Sri Lim stepped into uncharted territory, founding Tianjin Dreamland, the very first manufacturing joint venture established by a Malaysian entrepreneur in China.
At a time when few dared to venture in, he built fourteen joint ventures across major cities, including Shanghai, Dalian, Xi'an, Qingdao and Jiangyin, expanding into air‑conditioning, stainless steel and power generation.
Far more than building his own business, he became a trusted guide and bridge for the nation. Through the 1990s, he shared his insights, smoothed pathways, and helped leading Malaysian enterprises, including Robert Kuok's group, Maybank and PNB, navigate and succeed in the Chinese market.
His contributions to strengthening Malaysia–China economic ties earned him the appointment as Economic Advisor to Jiangyin City, Jiangsu Province, an honour rarely bestowed upon a foreign national.
From Mattresses To Malaysia's Digital City
Lim listed Dreamland Holdings Bhd on Bursa Malaysia in 1987, then diversified into steel as Kanzen Bhd, before restructuring his empire to focus on property, manufacturing, and financial services.
In July 1999, he acquired I-Berhad and set in motion his grandest vision yet: i-City.
Rising across 72 acres in Shah Alam with a RM12 billion gross development value, i-City is Malaysia's No. 1 Digital City, the first privately funded MSC Malaysia Cybercentre, an international park, and a unique tourism destination.
Ever ahead of his time, in 1995 he invested RM10 million to bring the Russian Mir Space Station exhibit to Malaysia, inspiring a generation of students in science and technology. In 2000 he partnered with ASUS to bridge the nation's digital divide; in 2016, he launched Malaysia's first IoT-enabled homes.
The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, officiated the opening of the DoubleTree by Hilton at Finance Avenue, i-City, in August 2022.
Today, under Lim's leadership, i-City has unveiled AI Living @ i-City, the world's first AI-enabled residential ecosystem, in partnership with China's AgiBot, weaving AI, robotics, and smart infrastructure into daily life.
Strategic alliances with Hilton, Wyndham, Central Group, and Maybank anchor its place as a regional tech and commerce hub.
"For me, the journey from furniture to mattresses, from manufacturing to China and from technology to digital cities has always been about anticipating how people will live next. Today, that instinct has led me to AI Living @ i-City, an attempt to imagine what the home of the future could become when AI and robotics move from screens into everyday life," Lim said.
Lim could have retired comfortably decades ago. Yet he remains at the helm, driven not by profit, but by purpose. He draws constant inspiration from Tunku Abdul Rahman's timeless words: "Without my country and my people, I am nothing."
He explains his choice simply: "I could retire and enjoy life. But I still want to contribute, in whatever way I can, to make Malaysia, and especially Selangor, a better place.

© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MEF: Foreign worker transit centre must be one-stop facility to ease arrivals
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A proposed foreign worker transit centre must operate as a coordinated one-stop facility to prevent delays and bottlenecks in the arrival process, the Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) said.
Its president, Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman, said the centre could improve coordination among agencies and ensure a smoother, more orderly process for incoming workers.
"It should be a coordinated one-stop arrangement where verification, documentation and related processes can be completed efficiently, reducing congestion and unnecessary delays for employers and incoming workers," he said.
Syed Hussain said safeguards were needed to ensure transit, screening and documentation processes were streamlined rather than creating new bottlenecks.
The aim, he added, was to enable foreign workers to complete all necessary procedures and report for work as soon as possible after arriving.
MEF said the proposed centre, together with the ministry's push to fully digitalise foreign worker recruitment applications, should be part of a broader effort to build a more integrated, transparent and efficient foreign worker management system.
On July 6, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the government was planning to
establish a foreign worker transit centre
that could accommodate between 1,000 and 2,000 workers to strengthen migrant labour management, improve security and ease airport congestion.
The move is aimed at tightening oversight of workers' movements and preventing them from being picked up by unauthorised parties.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Zahid calls for forensic audit into alleged wrongdoing at Felda
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has called for a forensic audit into alleged wrongdoings involving the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda).
Zahid said any suspected abuse of power, breach of trust or governance failures must be thoroughly investigated, adding that the probe should go beyond a conventional management audit.
"What is important is that it should not only involve a management audit, but a forensic audit must also be conducted," he told reporters after closing the 2026 World Islamic Tourism and Trade Expo at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur here today.
Zahid said Felda had faced serious problems for a long time and backed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in pursuing investigations into the agency.
"Let the prime minister take responsibility for carrying out the investigation, even though the former Felda chairman has been serving his sentence.
"If there is any abuse of power, breach of trust or failure to follow proper governance procedures, then in my view, a thorough investigation must be carried out," he said.
Zahid said those responsible for any wrongdoing should be brought to court if there was strong evidence against them, but cautioned against using investigations to humiliate individuals.
"Those responsible must, of course, be brought to court if there is strong evidence. But there should be no injustice or attempt to humiliate any individual," he said.
He also stressed that the welfare of Felda's 225,000 settlers and their families must remain protected, saying the wider Felda community spanning its first to fifth generations numbered at least 1.8 million people.
"We must look after them so that the interests and welfare of the Felda community continue to be properly safeguarded by the government," he said.
Anwar has stepped up scrutiny of Felda in recent weeks, saying that the agency was burdened with
nearly RM10 billion in debts and losses
after years of management failures and excessive political interference.
He said Felda had once been among the world's largest plantation organisations and generated billions of ringgit in profits annually before its financial position deteriorated.
Anwar said the government was paying RM980 million annually to cover Felda's financial obligations stemming from losses incurred under its previous management.
On Friday, Anwar said a special task force investigating Felda's management had begun its work and that he would wait for its complete findings before making an official announcement.
He said the
task force
would examine past problems as well as Felda's current management and future direction, with its findings to be made public once completed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid: BN to study grassroots sentiment before deciding on Melaka polls cooperation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional will study grassroots sentiment before deciding on any electoral cooperation for the coming Melaka election, its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
Zahid, who is also Umno president, said views at the grassroots level were mixed and would be taken into consideration before any decision was made.
"Grassroots sentiment is mixed. So we will conduct a detailed study.
"Jangan masuk ke lubuk di mana keli tidak boleh hidup ataupun ikan sepat tinggal tulang," (Don't enter a pool where even catfish cannot survive, or where the perch is left with nothing but bones), he told reporters after closing the World Islamic Tourism and Trade Expo at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur today.
Zahid said the issue of electoral cooperation would first be handled by Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
Any decision would subsequently be finalised by the Umno and BN leadership at the central level.
His remarks come amid differing views within Umno over the party's approach to the Melaka election, including whether BN should cooperate with Pakatan Harapan.
Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh said on Aug 18 that he would not contest in the coming state election if BN and PH cooperated in Melaka.
Zahid had earlier given Ab Rauf the
mandate to negotiate
with any political coalition ahead of the polls, with the outcome of any discussions to be referred to Umno's top leadership before being brought to the BN Supreme Council for final approval.
Rauf has said
Melaka BN is open to cooperation
with any party under a "BN Plus" formula, although he stressed that negotiations would not necessarily result in an agreement.
Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan said on Thursday that the party's political direction for the
Melaka election
would be discussed at the Supreme Council meeting on Aug 28.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia steps up Kalimantan firefighting as haze worsens in Sarawak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Indonesia is stepping up efforts to contain forest and land fires in Kalimantan, with President Prabowo Subianto overseeing firefighting operations.
Smoke from the fires has reached neighbouring Sarawak, where several areas have recorded unhealthy air quality.
Indonesian ambassador to Malaysia Raden Datuk Mohammad Iman Hascarya Kusumo said the government was monitoring developments and taking measures to prevent, detect, control and extinguish fires, particularly in fire-prone areas.
"Joint teams comprising central government agencies, the Indonesian National Police, the Indonesian National Armed Forces, regional governments and local communities are conducting firefighting operations, including water bombing and weather modification in affected areas.
"Challenges in the field, including the number of verified hotspots, weather conditions and the vast affected areas, are factored into firefighting efforts on the ground and from the air," he told the New Straits Times.
He was responding to growing concern in Malaysia over transboundary haze following worsening forest and land fires in Kalimantan.
On law enforcement, he said the Indonesian government was still verifying incidents and identifying those who might be responsible.
He also addressed allegations involving certain companies, including Malaysian-linked firms.
"Indonesia bases its position on verified data and findings of ongoing investigations, not assumptions," he said.
Four areas in Sarawak continued to record unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10am today, with Serian recording the highest at 192.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Kuching recorded 181, Sri Aman 176 and Samarahan 174.
Other areas in the state recorded moderate API readings below 100.
In the peninsula, Johan Setia recorded the highest reading at 158, followed by Sungai Petani (149) and Taiping (108).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NexG to resume expansion after government rules out Datasonic takeover
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: NexG Bhd will proceed with its domestic and international expansion plans after the government decided against taking over its unit Datasonic Technologies Sdn Bhd (DTSB).
NexG said the decision, announced by the National Security Council (NSC) on Saturday, reaffirmed the government's confidence in DTSB's ability to continue supplying Malaysia's high-security identity cards while maintaining security and reliability.
NexG and DTSB welcomed the decision, saying the subsidiary remained committed to upholding the highest standards of security, integrity and reliability after 27 years of supplying mission-critical identity solutions.
"The long-standing track record, supported by experienced local talent and in-house capabilities, reflects NexG's ability to continuously deliver mission-critical identity solutions securely and reliably," NexG said in a statement today.
The NSC had said the government would not take over DTSB, following recent reports that authorities were considering acquiring the company.
The council said the identity of Malaysians was one of the country's most important strategic assets and that the government would continue to safeguard its security and sovereignty through legislative, financial, governance and security frameworks.
The government's strategies, it added, would also seek to provide the best value for public spending.
NexG had previously disclosed that its preliminary internal assessment valued DTSB at RM7.5 billion following the government's request for an indicative price for a possible acquisition.
The company noted that the RM7.5 billion figure was not an independent valuation, agreed transaction value or firm offer.
DTSB currently holds a RM1.73 billion contract to supply passport booklets and polycarbonate biodata pages to the Immigration Department for six years from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2032.
It also has a RM732.72 million contract to supply raw cards and consumables to the National Registration Department over the same period.
NexG said DTSB would continue working with relevant government agencies to enhance the security features of Malaysia's identity cards and safeguard the identity of Malaysians.
"With the continuation of the raw identity card production contract for Malaysia, NexG can now continue with its strategic expansion plans in the domestic and international sectors, as previously planned.
"This will further expand NexG's wings and footprint as a high-tech technology company, in addition to being the leading manufacturer of high-security identity cards in Malaysia," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK's FTSE 100 clocks mild weekly gain as commodity-linked shares rise
Article:
LONDON: The FTSE 100 closed higher on Friday, boosted by gains in mining stocks, and managing to eke out a weekly gain at the end of a torrid week marred by persistent Middle East tensions and growing inflation worries.
The blue-chip FTSE 100 rose 0.6 per cent to 10,816.6 points, also clocking a 0.6 per cent rise for the week. The midcap FTSE 250 climbed 0.9 per cent but marked its first weekly decline in six.
* Precious and industrial metal miners rose as gold and copper prices edged higher against a dollar weakened by the U.S. Treasury's bond buyback move. Antofagasta and Endeavour Mining rose 5.4 per cent and 4.1 per cent, respectively, leading gains in the FTSE 100.
* US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Thursday he may further increase the government's repurchases of Treasuries, in an effort to support a government debt market that had begun to balk after the previous day's surprise plan to double buybacks.
* Global stocks were set for their biggest weekly fall since mid-July, as strain in global bond markets showed little sign of abating.
* Iran said that its response to any new US threats would be "devastating" after Washington pledged to impose the toughest financial penalties in history with the aim of toppling the Iranian leadership.
* British retail sales fell back as expected in July after a surge in June when hot weather boosted demand for fans and air conditioners, while supermarkets offered promotions alongside the men's soccer World Cup, official figures showed.
* Separately, Britain's services sector, the engine of its economy, grew unexpectedly this month, according to a survey, adding to signs of resilience despite the conflict in the Middle East.
* British telecom services provider Gamma Communications gained 11.6 per cent after it said it was in early talks with the Netherlands-based Waterland Private Equity Investments over a possible takeover.
* Energy services firm Hunting sank 14.5 per cent as it lowered its annual core profit forecast after delays to a major Kuwait Oil Company tender process.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi: 2027 Budget to put greater focus on cost of living
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will place greater emphasis on addressing cost-of-living issues more comprehensively in the 2027 Budget, taking into account the unsettled global geopolitical situation.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said budget preparations would also consider external factors, including global crude oil price movements.
"Overall, the government's focus in the 2027 Budget will include ensuring cost-of-living issues are addressed more comprehensively, taking into account the geopolitical situation, which remains unresolved at this time.
"So, factors such as crude oil prices, which are usually one of the benchmarks, will be among the considerations," he said.
He spoke to reporters after launching the 2026 Kembara Merdeka Jalur Gemilang X JAGO programme for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya at the Taman Seri Sentosa Market today.
Fahmi said the budget would also prioritise projects capable of resolving public issues quickly, while attracting more domestic and international investment to support the 13th Malaysia Plan.
For the Communications Ministry, he said a key priority was expanding internet access, particularly in remote areas.
He added that the ministry was looking into media sustainability issues and incentives to attract international events and film productions to Malaysia.
"Incentives such as the Concerts and Events in Malaysia Incentive (CIME) and Filming in Malaysia Incentive (FIMI) can attract more investors to Malaysia.
"These are currently being discussed at the ministry level following feedback received from the Finance Ministry," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia welcomes more Chinese investments, business: Prabowo
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia welcomes more Chinese enterprises to invest and do business in the country, will continue to provide a sound business environment for Chinese companies, and opposes any ill-intentioned instigation and hype, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto has said here, reported Xinhua.
Prabowo made the remarks on Friday while meeting with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, and Defence Minister Dong Jun at his official residence.
Prabowo positively evaluated the role and achievements of the Indonesia-China Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue Mechanism and the 2+2 dialogue mechanism.
He said that China has successfully lifted hundreds of millions of people out of poverty and achieved great accomplishments in the economic, scientific and technological, and military fields, setting a good example for Global South countries to learn from.
Prabowo said China treats Indonesia as an equal with mutual respect, and provides Indonesia with valuable confidence and support.
Indonesia looks forward to deepening all-round strategic cooperation with China in areas such as politics, the economy, science and technology, the Indonesian president said, noting that he expects to attend the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen in November this year to further enhance strategic communication and collaboration with the Chinese side.
For his part, Wang said that under the president's leadership, Indonesia has overcome various difficulties in recent years and its national construction has entered into a stage of rapid development.
Both the Chinese and Indonesian governments are committed to developing the economy and delivering benefits to their people. No force can stop the continuous rise of developing countries such as China and Indonesia, Wang said.
Noting that China and Indonesia have obvious complementary advantages, Wang said China is a reliable, long-term and stable partner in Indonesia's national development process.
Wang said China has the ability and willingness to deepen cooperation with Indonesia to help Indonesia turn its resources into development momentum, accelerate the pace of industrialisation and modernisation, and bring more tangible benefits to its people.
The development of human society has proved that openness leads to continuous progress, while isolation only results in backwardness, Wang said.
The more turbulent the world becomes and the more complex and severe external challenges grow, the more China and Indonesia should strengthen solidarity, deepen mutual trust and support, uphold openness and cooperation, safeguard common interests, achieve their respective national development, and set a model of cooperation for Global South countries, Wang noted.
China stands ready to work with Indonesia to earnestly implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, as well as the outcomes of the first Conference of China-Indonesia Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue Mechanism and the second ministerial meeting of the 2+2 dialogue mechanism, Wang said.
The two sides will comprehensively advance cooperation in areas including politics, economy, energy and mineral resources, military and security, so as to continuously inject fresh impetus into their respective national development and rejuvenation, as well as make positive contributions to regional peace and stability, Wang said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Civil Defence man dies after king cobra bite during demonstration
Article:
TEMERLOH: A Civil Defence Force (APM) personnel died early today after being bitten by a king cobra during a demonstration yesterday.
Sergeant (PA) Muhamad Muazam Shah Kamardin, 39, of the Temerloh APM office, died at Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (Hoshas) here at 1.50am.
Pahang APM director Colonel Che Adam A. Rahman said Muazam Shah died while receiving treatment.
His remains will be taken to the Kampung Bukit Kelulut Mosque for funeral prayers before burial in the village.
In the 10.50am incident yesterday, Muazam Shah and an APM team had been invited to a programme at Taman Temerloh Jaya, where he demonstrated his reptile-handling skills on stage.
"He was bitten on the right middle fingernail and immediately left the hall to wash his hands. He passed out outside and was taken to the Hoshas emergency unit, where he was given antivenom," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No Malaysians injured in Narathiwat blasts, arson attacks
Article:
KOTA BARU: No Malaysians were injured after at least 11 locations in Thailand's southern border province of Narathiwat were hit by a series of security incidents, including explosions, arson attacks and the burning of vehicle tyres last night.
Narathiwat provincial police commander Major General Prayong Kotsakha said two Thai citizens were injured in the incidents.
He said the incidents, which began at 8pm, involved several areas in Narathiwat, including locations near the Malaysia-Thailand border.
"Following the incidents, a curfew was imposed from 10.15pm last night until 6am today.
"Today, the situation has returned to normal and no curfew is being imposed," he told the New Straits Times.
He said the curfew was necessary to allow authorities to secure the affected areas, inspect incident sites and prevent further attacks.
"With the curfew in place, security personnel can carry out inspections and investigations more effectively while ensuring the safety of residents," he said.
Security forces were deployed to secure the affected areas and investigate the attacks.
Among the affected locations were Ban Buket Bue Raoh, the Bongor Subdistrict Administrative Organisation in Rangae district, and Ban Thamniap in Muang Narathiwat district.
A roadside shelter in front of the Narathiwat Provincial Transport Office's Sungai Golok branch in Ban Kwalao Sira, Pasemat subdistrict, along the Sungai Golok-Muno route, was also targeted.
In Sungai Golok, authorities stepped up security following an explosion in front of the transport office and in areas bordering Kelantan.
Meanwhile, the Internal Security Operations Command Region 4 Forward Command urged the public to exercise caution, avoid incident sites and controlled areas, and refrain from approaching or moving suspicious objects.
The public was also advised against sharing real-time photographs, videos or locations of security personnel, as such information could compromise security operations and efforts to track down those responsible.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN open to seat allocation with BN to ensure victories, says Takiyuddin
Article:
KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional is open to negotiating seat allocations with Umno to strengthen the opposition's chances in state and federal elections.
PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the coalition was willing to give up certain seats to Umno if cooperation could help secure victories in states where both parties had support.
"There is no problem. We can give our seats to Umno for it to win states, whether in state elections or the 16th General Election (GE16)," he said during a ceramah on current issues here last night.
The Pas secretary-general said the cooperation could be based on the principle of 'muafakat' (consensus), with both parties discussing the best arrangement according to their respective strengths.
"For example, in Negri Sembilan, if we win 25 seats after cooperating with Barisan Nasional, then in Melaka, if we combine our strengths, how many seats could we win?
"Perhaps in Kelantan and Terengganu, we will discuss. This is what we call bermuafakat," he added.
He said Pas, a PN component party, had previously shown its willingness to work with Umno and Barisan Nasional.
Takiyuddin said Pas had agreed to let Umno contest 25 of the 36 state seats in Negri Sembilan, while PN would contest the remaining 11 under an electoral cooperation arrangement.
He said such cooperation reflected the party's focus on securing the best outcome for the people, rather than serving political interests.
"We will continue with this approach. Otherwise, how could PN win all 28 state seats in Terengganu?
"Similarly, Pas and Angkatan Perpaduan Ummah won all 39 state seats in Terengganu in 1990.
"Terengganu has eight parliamentary seats and we won all eight. No other party, including Pakatan Harapan or Barisan Nasional, won any," he said.
Takiyuddin said Pas and PN's strength in states such as Terengganu and Kelantan would be considered in future seat allocation talks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Businessman charged with assaulting Vietnamese woman at KL club
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A businessman has been charged with voluntarily causing hurt to a Vietnamese woman who was allegedly assaulted at a club here earlier this month.
Wangsa Maju police chief Assistant Commissioner Annas Sulaiman said police received a report on Aug 6 and investigated the case under Sections 323 and 506 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt and criminal intimidation.
"The investigation paper was referred to the deputy public prosecutor on Aug 11, with instructions to charge the accused under Section 323.
"The accused, a 36-year-old businessman, Tan Zhie Yang, was subsequently charged at the Jalan Duta court on Aug 13," he said in a statement.
Previously, Kepong MP Lim Lip Eng called on Bukit Aman to reopen investigations into the alleged assault of 28-year-old Vietnamese woman Dao Thi Kim Tra at a club on Aug 4.
Dao claimed she was assaulted by two men in a VIP room, suffering injuries to her left eye, head and stomach, and alleged that one of the men threatened her with a gun.
She lodged a police report at the Wangsa Maju police station on Aug 6, claiming only one suspect was detained before being released two days later.S

Title: Malaysia tech sector poised for extended AI-driven bull run into FY27
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's technology sector is poised for a sustained bull run into the second half (2H) of 2026, supported by accelerating earnings growth, robust order books and stronger factory loadings, RHB Research said.
The firm's analyst Lee Meng Horng said recent ground checks across the technology supply chain reinforced the firm's high-conviction view that the sector remains firmly in an upcycle, which could extend into financial year 2027 (FY27).
"This upcycle could well be extended into FY27 – supported by robust factory loadings, expanding orderbooks, and bullish customer forecasts amid accelerating AI demand and recovery across other segments," he said in a research note.
Lee expects most technology companies to deliver stronger year-on-year (YoY) and quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) earnings, underpinned by healthy backlogs, high loadings, steady project execution and accelerating billings.
The positive earnings trajectory is expected to continue into 2H, aided by the seasonal ramp-up in the second half and a favourable foreign exchange tailwind on a quarterly basis.
RHB Research maintained its "Overweight" call on the technology sector, with Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd, Pentamaster Corp Bhd and CTOS Digital Bhd as its top picks.
Lee expects the Kuala Lumpur Technology Index to continue outperforming as sector earnings growth accelerates from the second quarter of 2026.
He noted that the sector is trading at about 27 times forward price-to-earnings (P/E), or one standard deviation above its five-year mean, against forecast FY26-FY27 earnings growth of more than 30 per cent.
Greater upside is seen among laggards and second-tier names, where earnings recovery and operational improvements have yet to be fully reflected in valuations, Lee said.
Meanwhile, the AI-led upcycle is expected to remain a key driver of semiconductor demand.
The Semiconductor Industry Association has raised its 2026 semiconductor market forecast to US$1.5 trillion, while projecting a further 27 per cent growth in 2027 as AI deployment continues.
Semiconductor Equipment and Materials International also expects semiconductor equipment spending to increase 10 per cent YoY to US$138 billion in 2026, driven by capacity expansion in leading-edge logic, dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and advanced packaging.
Malaysia is also benefiting from the upcycle, with electrical and electronics (E&E) exports jumping 43 per cent YoY to RM468 billion in the first half of this year, contributing more than half of the country's total export growth.
"Rising FY26 and FY27 capital expenditure estimates for (major US technology companies) the Magnificent 7 further reinforce expectations of a sustained AI infrastructure buildout and industry upcycle," Lee said.
He said rapid adoption of generative AI and hyperscale data centres is also creating structural demand for advanced packaging, power semiconductors and high-speed networking.
He said higher computing intensity and rack power densities are creating bottlenecks in power, thermal management and bandwidth, accelerating the adoption of technologies such as silicon carbide and gallium nitride for power conversion.
At the same time, 2.5D and 3D advanced packaging, high-bandwidth memory, silicon photonics and co-packaged optics are gaining traction as the industry seeks higher computing density, lower latency and improved energy efficiency.
However, Lee flagged several near-term risks, including elevated memory prices that could weigh on consumer electronics demand by increasing costs for smartphones, personal computers and automotive electronics.
Other risks include geopolitical tensions, foreign exchange volatility, cost-driven margin pressure and intermittent order delays arising from component shortages.
Potential interest rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve could also put pressure on technology sector valuations, it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang Occupational Safety Dept probes worker's death at Juru telecom tower
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Occupational Safety and Health Department is investigating the death of a telecommunications worker following an accident at a tower in Juru.
The department said it was notified of the workplace accident involving the worker, who died on Aug 16.
The incident occurred around 4.45pm on July 11 at a telecommunications tower in Kampung Juru, Simpang Ampat.
The victim was believed to have been carrying out corrective maintenance work when the accident occurred.
The department said its initial investigation on Aug 19 found that the victim was believed to have fallen while descending the tower from a height of about 63cm after passing through a tower plinth.
"Following the investigation, a letter of direction was issued to the relevant party to submit documents and information related to the accident for further investigation," it said in a statement today.
The investigation is being conducted under Sections 15(1), 17(1) and 18B of the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1994, as well as relevant occupational safety and health regulations.
The department said it took all workplace accidents seriously and reminded employers of their responsibility to ensure workers' safety, health and welfare.
It also urged employers to conduct risk assessments, maintain safe work areas and access routes, and implement appropriate safety and risk-control measures.S
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fitch keeps Poland rating at 'A-', cites fiscal risks in negative outlook
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Fitch retained Poland's sovereign credit rating at "A-" on Friday, citing the country's resilient economy and strong external finances relative to similarly rated peers, while maintaining a "negative" outlook due to a lack of strong fiscal consolidation.
Here are some more details:
* The rating action comes as the nation's budget deficit widened to 141.1 billion zlotys (US$38.19 billion) at the end of July, compared with 123.7 billion zlotys (US$33.48 billion) at the end of June.
* The agency expects the country's fiscal deficit to narrow marginally to 6.7 per cent of GDP in 2027, above its February forecast of 6.2 per cent, and flagged risks of additional spending ahead of elections.
* Fitch said revenue would be constrained by weaker economic growth and a lower corporate tax rate for banks, while the scope for offsetting measures remains limited by the risk of presidential vetoes.
* Poland is witnessing a political gridlock between the Brussels-oriented government led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk and the conservative-nationalist President Karol Nawrocki. Last month, Nawrocki referred a bill introducing a windfall tax on oil and gas companies' profits to the country's constitutional court.
* Poland's second-quarter GDP growth rose to 3.8 per cent from 3.5 per cent in the first quarter, in line with forecasts.
* Fitch expects GDP growth of 3.3 per cent in 2026, with investment supported by EU Recovery and Resilience Facility projects and high defence spending, partly offsetting slower private consumption as real wage growth moderates.
* The comments come days after the government unveiled plans to cut income taxes for middle-income earners and raise corporate taxes for larger companies from next year. Finance Minister Andrzej Domanski said he expected a "slightly positive" reception of the proposed changes from rating agencies.
* "This is very good news. In the agency's view, the Polish economy remains strong, resilient, and well-diversified," Domanski wrote on the X platform following the Fitch announcement.
* "However, rating agencies are signaling risks to public finances. (...) Fitch explicitly states that the record number of presidential vetoes limits the ability to implement effective economic policy."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak ties economic growth to ESG goals
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak has cemented its standing as a pioneer in aligning economic expansion with environmental, social and governance goals.
The state recently reclaimed the Best Sustainability Initiative (Destination) honour at the 2026 Meetings & Conventions Asia Stella Awards, two years after first winning the honour in 2024.
The recognition validates how the state's Legacy Impact Framework has redefined standards for responsible business events across the region, embedding sustainable development at the intersection of commerce, community welfare and environmental stewardship.
"Sustainability must go beyond the environment to include social and economic progress, while legacy ensures that the value created through business events can continue long after an event has ended," said Datuk Sri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah, Minister for Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Sarawak.
The framework anchors Sarawak's business events sector to two core blueprints, its post-Covid-19 Development Strategy 2030 and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.
"Winning this award for the second time demonstrates the importance of sustainability and legacy to Sarawak's business events strategy and wider development," he said in a statement.
Since its debut win, Sarawak has translated vision into measurable action, rolling out education, standardised measurement and industry-wide programmes that embed legacy thinking across the full event lifecycle.
"This recognition reflects the collective effort behind Sarawak's legacy journey," said Datuk Hii Chang Kee, Deputy State Secretary (Operation) and chairman of Business Events Sarawak (BESarawak).
"What began with advocacy is gaining greater participation across the industry. Legacy is ultimately about shaping the future together, with government, industry, organisers and communities each playing a role in creating shared and meaningful outcomes," he said.
With global endorsement in hand, Sarawak is now raising the bar once again. The next phase will drive widespread adoption across the ecosystem: standardising how legacy outcomes are planned, measured, and delivered, and building industry capability to turn promise into permanent value.
"Legacy impact is gaining greater relevance, not only for Sarawak but across the Asia Pacific business events industry," said Jason Tan Chin Foo, chief executive officer of BESarawak.
"Our next phase is to drive greater adoption across the ecosystem, ensuring that legacy outcomes are consistently planned, measured and demonstrated," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hit by Trump tariffs, Quebec loses appetite for quick separation from Canada
Article:
MONTREAL: When US President Donald Trump levied 50 per cent tariffs on Canadian steel in June last year, a steel factory in Canada's mostly French-speaking province of Quebec lost about a third of its orders for bolts and fasteners in less than a week.
The factory owner – The Heico Companies – froze hiring, closed a plant in the region and laid off several dozen people, said David Jeannotte, an operations director, whose own brother lost his job.
The cuts were part of 140 layoffs by the company, mainly in Quebec. The factory's troubles reflect broader anxiety over the fallout from Trump's trade war in Quebec, which is due to hold a provincial election by Oct 5.
But while some previous economic slowdowns in the province prompted an increase in separatist sentiment, polls show that this time around, support for an independent Quebec is at its lowest level in decades, at about 30 per cent.
"As long as Trump will be in his chair, I don't feel that we even need to talk about that," Jeannotte said.
Others in the region are echoing Jeannotte's concerns, saying the threat Trump poses to Canada means the best way to preserve Quebec's unique French culture is to stay within Canada – at least for now.
Trump's threats to make Canada the 51st state and the whiplash from his tariff policy have spurred an outpouring of Canadian patriotism in Quebec, a province that regularly threatens to break away and has had two previous referendums on the issue.
As the country's only majority French-speaking province, Quebec has a long-established separatist movement that argues independence from Canada is the best way to protect its distinct culture and language.
Quebec has never formally signed the Canadian Constitution and separatists argue French Canadians are often overlooked by the English-dominated majority.
CAMPAIGN OF FEAR
The separatist Parti Quebecois currently holds a slim lead in provincial election polls and a win would mark the party's return to power after a dozen years.
But analysts say a vote for the party would be more about disappointment with the ruling party than an endorsement of the PQ's independence platform.
While the PQ is committed to a third independence referendum if it wins, leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon vowed that won't happen while Trump is president, a tacit recognition of falling support for independence.
Quebec narrowly voted to stay in Canada in a 1995 referendum, spurring a national reckoning that resulted in the federal government asking the Supreme Court to clarify the legal procedure for separation.
On Tuesday, Plamondon said in a post on X that deciding Quebec's political fate "must not be hijacked by the upheaval of American politics, the outbursts of an unpredictable president or by a campaign of fear."
The explicit acknowledgement of the risk Trump poses to Quebec's independence movement aligns with a broader pattern in which the US president's policies and rhetoric, including his stance on Greenland, have undermined separatist causes elsewhere.
In both Scotland and Catalonia, efforts to break away from the United Kingdom and Spain have been complicated by uncertainty stemming from Trump's tariff threats and criticism of NATO.
A delayed Quebec sovereignty vote would be one less headache for Liberal Prime Minister Mark Carney, who himself upended polls favouring the Conservatives to win a national election last year after promising to be a tough negotiator with Trump.
Carney faces another separatist movement in oil-rich Alberta, which has its own referendum scheduled for mid-October.
While conservative Alberta's burgeoning independence movement aligns with Trump's brand of conservatism, Quebecers have largely supported the rest of Canada in pressing back against the US president's tariffs and threats of annexation.
"Postponing a referendum is unfortunately a choice we have to accept," said Stéphane Bédard, a former interim leader of the PQ.
"Quebec is stronger than it's ever been, but the external factor of Trump has created a lot of insecurity, so we have to be realistic."
Trump is more disliked in Quebec, arguably the country's most progressive province, than anywhere else in Canada.
According to August data from the pollster Angus Reid, only 10 per cent of Quebecers have a favourable view of the president, and even a deal to lower tariffs is unlikely to reverse public opinion.
"Trump represents everything that Quebec has fought against for the last 60 years in terms of creating a modern, progressive society," said Jonathan Kalles, former Quebec adviser to ex-Prime Minister Justin Trudeau.
Trump's conservative policies as well as his administration's comments that the province's French language requirements are a "trade irritant" are both unpopular.
The financial impact from his policies is also strongly felt in Quebec and economists note the province is among the worst hit by Trump's tariffs, given its concentration of industries like steel and aluminium.
A March report from the Bank of Montreal estimated Quebec's economy would grow about 1.0 per cent this year, compared to more than 2.0 per cent for Alberta and Saskatchewan.
Jeannotte, of a factory near Montreal, said that before Trump levied tariffs on Canadian steel, about 90 per cent of its products were destined for the US, with its bolts used in New York's Empire State Building.
Jeannotte said some staffers work without pay on some days and others have voluntarily reduced their hours.
AT THE NEGOTIATING TABLE
Still, some Quebec separatists say independence remains critical, even now.
Marie-Anne Alepin, president of the separatist Société Saint-Jean-Baptiste de Montréal, said Carney's decision to eliminate a tax that helps finance Canadian programming would cut funding for Quebec's French-language productions, highlighting that as an example of why the province should become independent.
Ottawa has pledged to replace the tax with government funding.
"Canada is not capable of defending Quebec's interests," Alepin said. "(Quebec) has to be at the negotiating table and to do that, we have to be a country."
Vincent Rainville, a fourth-generation Quebec dairy farmer who owns more than 250 cows, disagreed, saying Trump's policies have complicated efforts to strengthen Quebec's economy and that a national response is required. Nearly half of Canada's dairy farms are in Quebec.
"It's not just Quebec, it's all of Canada and all our industries that have been affected," he said. "If I supported an independent Quebec, I would not want to talk about that policy now."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: OSK Property partners RHB Bank to extend home and renovation loan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: OSK Property Holdings Bhd has partnered with RHB Bank Bhd to extend the RHB Home and Renovation Loan to eligible purchasers of selected under-construction landed properties developed by OSK Property.
The property arm of OSK Group said in a statement that the collaboration marked RHB's first property-developer partnership for the solution, which was previously available to eligible purchasers of completed and subsale properties.
It said the solution will now enable purchasers of selected under-construction landed homes priced at RM300,000 and above at OSK Yarra Park and OSK Taman Lang Aman in Sungai Petani, Kedah and OSK Iringan Bayu in Seremban, Negri Sembilan to apply for and package their housing and renovation loans together at the point of property purchase.
"This allows eligible purchasers to plan their overall homeownership and renovation funding needs upfront, instead of arranging separate renovation funding only after their homes are completed.
"The renovation loan will subsequently be disbursed progressively for approved renovation works after the property is completed and the applicable requirements have been fulfilled, subject to RHB's credit assessment and terms and conditions," it said.
OSK Property said the solution provides an additional loan margin of up to 30 per cent of the lower of the property's selling price or latest market value, comprising the renovation loan and, where applicable, Mortgage Reducing Term Assurance (MRTA), Credit Life Term Assurance (CLTA) and Finance Entry Cost (FEC), on top of a housing loan margin of up to 90 per cent.
The company added that the tenure is up to 35 years or until the customer reaches 70 years old, whichever is earlier.
OSK Property chief executive officer Chu Wai Lune said the collaboration offers eligible purchasers a more seamless financing option that supports both home purchase and renovation needs in one journey.
"We are also encouraged that RHB has chosen OSK Property as its first property-developer partner for this solution, which we see as a strong reflection of its confidence in the quality, value and standards of the homes we deliver.
"This partnership reflects our shared commitment to making the homeownership experience more practical, accessible and meaningful for customers," he said.
Meanwhile, RHB Bank managing director, group community banking, Jeffrey Ng Eow Oo said the collaboration enables eligible purchasers to have both their housing and renovation loan requirements assessed and packaged upfront when purchasing the property, providing greater clarity and convenience in planning the overall cost of homeownership.
"While the renovation loan will only be disbursed after the property is completed and the relevant requirements have been fulfilled, packaging both components upfront enables customers to plan ahead from the point of purchase.
"This allows RHB to support them more seamlessly, from purchasing their property to transforming it into a home that reflects their needs and aspirations, resulting in a holistic customer experience," he said.
According to OSK Property, the collaboration forms part of its continued efforts to enhance the customer journey through practical lifestyle and homeownership solutions and reinforces the company's focus on creating long-term value for purchasers by connecting quality homes with value-added offerings that support modern living.

Title: Pas says it's not ignoring Tabung Haji RCI
Article:
KOTA BARU: Pas has denied claims that it is prioritising foreign policy issues over the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the party's questions on foreign policy, particularly on China and Taiwan, did not mean it was neglecting the Tabung Haji RCI.
He said Pas had the right, as a political party, to express its views and disagree with government policies, including on foreign affairs.
"We do not necessarily have to agree with everything concerning the government's foreign policy.
"The issue involving Taiwan and China concerns foreign policy. As a political party in Malaysia, we have the right to state our views and disagree with a particular policy," he told reporters here last night.
Takiyuddin said Malaysia's foreign policy had traditionally been based on the principles of being free, neutral and non-interventionist in the internal affairs of other countries.
He cited the administration of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, saying Malaysia at the time did not interfere in the China-Taiwan issue or the Russia-related conflict.
"Instead, Malaysia took the approach of maintaining relations with the parties involved in disputes to help achieve a resolution," he said.
Takiyuddin said this raised the question of whether the government's current approach represented a new foreign policy.
"The government needs to explain this.
"Tun Dr Mahathir himself had faced opposition from certain parties and countries which viewed interference in the affairs of other nations as a form of intervention," he said.
On the Tabung Haji RCI, Takiyuddin said Pas had its own strategy and was waiting for the appropriate time to debate the matter.
"If there are no other developments, the matter will be debated in October.
"We already know the narrative being put forward by Pakatan Harapan regarding the Tabung Haji RCI.
"So, wait until October because we will debate the Tabung Haji RCI then, including matters concerning the policies and issues that have arisen," he said.
Earlier, it was
reported
that Pas had been called out by PKR Youth information chief Danish Hairudin for 'lecturing' Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on foreign policy, instead of focusing on issues raised in the RCI report on Tabung Haji.
In a Facebook post, Danish said Pas appeared overly eager to advise Anwar on Malaysia's diplomatic position over the China-Taiwan issue.
